17.0.0.en: He declares that the sin of the tribe of Judah, meaning the whole southern kingdom, is engraved on their hearts; it is written with a pen of iron, that is, a strong one able to engrave in stones, and likewise with the point of a diamond, a strong mineral able to engrave in metals also. In sum, sin is fixed in them and in their heart, that is, in their feelings and inner intentions, and is not merely a slipping into a superficial sin.

17.0.1.en: Their sin also appears on their altars, that is, the pagan worship and the sacrifices offered on the altars of the idols.

17.1.0.en: Whilst their children remember: customary speech; as a man remembers his sons, so their talk of the worship of idols had become, which they had grown accustomed to.

17.1.1.en: Their groves: the plural of “pole,” a tall piece of wood planted in the ground at which worship is offered to the goddess of fertility, one of the pagan goddesses.

17.1.2.en: Hills: mounds. The tribe of Judah was accustomed to worship idols by setting up altars or poles for them; likewise they offered the worship of idols under the green trees and offered this worship also upon the hills. In sum, this verse declares the spread of pagan worship among God's people everywhere.

17.2.0.en: Thy borders: your boundaries. God warns His people of destruction and plunder when their enemies attack them and take away their wealth, seizing it from their fortified cities however strong they are, like a towering mountain, because they worshiped idols on these mountains and everywhere.

17.3.0.en: Thus God's people give up their land and their heritage, so they leave them, that is, disown them, and go into captivity. The real cause of the captivity is not the cruelty of the enemies but the sin of Judah; therefore God allowed the enemies to attack him. And when the captivity took place, God's people went to become slaves serving the Babylonians, and this was God's anger because of the sin of Judah, which kindled God's anger against them, an anger that continues forever if they do not repent of their sins; for God's anger continues against sinners who have not repented and is completed on the Day of Judgment, when they go to eternal torment.

17.3.1.en: Sin is what separates you from God and deprives you of His blessings and brings every wrath upon you. So do not be deceived by its pleasure, for it passes away and leaves in you a great bitterness; and if you fall, hasten to repentance to rescue yourself, for our God is compassionate and merciful.

17.3.3.en: 5- Thus saith the LORD; Cursed be the man that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm, and whose heart departeth from the LORD. 6- For he shall be like the heath in the desert, and shall not see when good cometh; but shall inhabit the parched places in the wilderness, in a salt land and not inhabited. 7- Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, and whose hope the LORD is. 8- For he shall be as a tree planted by the waters, and that spreadeth out her roots by the river, and shall not see when heat cometh, but her leaf shall be green; and shall not be careful in the year of drought, neither shall cease from yielding fruit.

17.4.0.en: His arm: his strength, because man works with the arm and his strength is shown by it.

17.4.1.en: God warns the kingdom of Judah against relying on men and their strength, for these lose God's help and are cursed by Him, because they have turned away from Him and rejected Him.

17.5.0.en: The heath: a dry plant without fruit that appears in the desert.

17.5.2.en: The parched places: the hot land, that is, one with no plants or fruits, which means the absence of fruit in the man.

17.5.3.en: A salt land: salty land unfit for cultivation.

17.5.4.en: God's people relied on men, as when they tried to rely on Egypt to fortify themselves against Assyria and Babylon instead of relying on God, so they became a dry people without fruit like the heath in the desert: when the plants give fruit and good, it does not give, and it dwells in an uninhabited land, like the salt land or the extremely hot one. The meaning is that whoever does not trust in God does not enjoy spiritual fruits in his life and becomes despised by people and loses material blessings as well.

17.6.0.en: On the contrary, whoever trusts in God receives many blessings in his life, whether spiritual or material.

17.7.0.en: He likens the man who trusts in God to a tree planted beside a stream of water, which spreads its roots in the ground and finds water sufficient for it, so that it does not suffer from the heat or the drought that comes upon all plants, because it is planted beside the stream of water. The stream of water here means God, on whom His children rely, so they are not troubled by the afflictions of life.

17.7.1.en: Seek God before every work and you will feel His help, and your heart will no longer be troubled however much afflictions come upon you, because He rescues you from them and is even glorified in you through them.

17.8.s.en: (3) The reward of the righteous and the wicked

17.8.0.en: God warns His children in the kingdom of Judah not to walk in evil with their wicked hearts, lest their heart become desperately wicked, that is, bitter.

17.8.1.en: Seek God before every work and you will feel His help, and your heart will no longer be troubled however much afflictions come upon you.

17.9.0.en: God declares of Himself that He is the One who knows the secrets of hearts, and therefore He punishes His wicked people with captivity, that perhaps they may repent, and rewards His obedient children with peace and joy.

17.10.0.en: The partridge: a wild bird with long legs and a red beak that lived in Palestine and laid its eggs in nests on the ground and not on trees.

17.10.1.en: The partridge used to sit on and sleep upon the eggs of other birds, and when the eggs hatched, it would produce chicks foreign to it that soon left it, so that it gained nothing from all its labor. This bird is like one who gets riches by unlawful means, for they are lost to him afterward, whether by their loss or by his death, so he gains nothing from what he obtained.

17.10.2.en: It seems that this verse was a proverb that people repeated, and God used it here to forbid the love of money and the acquiring of it by unlawful means such as theft and exploitation.

17.11.0.en: On the other side, God declares that His holy place in His house is great and high above all the earthly things with which the people of the world are occupied and in which they waste their lives.

17.12.0.en: Whoever forsakes the holy God loses his purity and exaltation and loses his eternal heavenly place, and his life clings to the dust from which he was taken, so he is written in it, that is, he dies and his life ends in passing earthly things. And Jeremiah directs the attention of God's people to the fact that their hope is God, that they may come out of their material afflictions and their preoccupation with sin and earthly things, for He is the fountain of true living water, and not riches and money.

17.12.1.en: Do not forget that you are a child of heaven, because your Father is heavenly; so do not be occupied with passing material things and do not be troubled by the afflictions of life, because God is able to rescue you from them, and you will remain like Him at all times.

17.13.0.en: Jeremiah speaks as a servant on behalf of his people, declaring that he is a sinner in need of God's healing, and with humility also declares his personal need for healing, and in this way he is an example to his people in returning to God by repentance. He asks God to heal him from the wounds of sin and rescue him from all his troubles, so that he may continue to praise God and enjoy constant prayer with Him.

17.14.0.en: At the time when Jeremiah offers repentance before God, the people deny the existence of God and His work, and say of Him that He does not carry out His word and does not punish the one who sins; indeed they mock and say, “Where is the word of the LORD? let it come now,” if it is true.

17.15.0.en: I have not withdrawn: I have not abandoned my place as a shepherd of the people.

17.15.1.en: But Jeremiah was not affected by the words of the people who doubted God's work, and continued to shepherd his people and warn them to repent; and in all this he follows God and takes refuge in Him, for God is his leader in all his service. And in the spirit of fatherhood he did not wish that God's wrath should come upon his people to punish them for their sins, that they might know that His word is true and so answer their mockery.

17.15.2.en: But he wishes that God would be longsuffering until his people repent, and God bears witness against himself that he asked in his prayers to God for repentance for his people, besides that God knows his heart and feelings and fatherhood toward the people.

17.16.0.en: Jeremiah asks for himself and for all the people God's tenderness and mercy, that He not repay them for their sins with fear and affliction, because He is their refuge in all their afflictions.

17.17.0.en: The day of evil: the day of affliction.

17.17.1.en: In faith he asks the help of God, who reassures him, and at the same time frightens his enemies and defeats them and crushes them before him; so even if affliction comes upon him from the enemies, God is able to deliver him from their hands and crush them. This was fulfilled in God's keeping Jeremiah in the faith throughout his life, while those of the people who troubled him were terrified before Babylon, and the Babylonians too, their kingdom passed away after years at the hand of the kingdom of the Medes and Persians.

17.17.2.en: Be confident in the power of your God, who protects you however much the wars of the demons rise against you and however much you fall; He is able to raise you up and defeat them before you, and even to gladden your heart with His consolations until you obtain glory in the Kingdom of Heaven.

17.17.4.en: 19- Thus said the LORD unto me; Go and stand in the gate of the children of the people, whereby the kings of Judah come in, and by the which they go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem; 20- And say unto them, Hear ye the word of the LORD, ye kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that enter in by these gates: 21- Thus saith the LORD; Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem; 22- Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers. 23- But they obeyed not, neither inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, nor receive instruction. 24- And it shall come to pass, if ye diligently hearken unto me, saith the LORD, to bring in no burden through the gates of this city on the sabbath day, but hallow the sabbath day, to do no work therein;

17.17.5.en: 25- Then shall there enter into the gates of this city kings and princes sitting upon the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, they, and their princes, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: and this city shall remain for ever.

17.17.6.en: 26- And they shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places about Jerusalem, and from the land of Benjamin, and from the plain, and from the mountains, and from the south, bringing burnt offerings, and sacrifices, and meat offerings, and incense, and bringing sacrifices of praise, unto the house of the LORD.

17.17.7.en: 27- But if ye will not hearken unto me to hallow the sabbath day, and not to bear a burden, even entering in at the gates of Jerusalem on the sabbath day; then will I kindle a fire in the gates thereof, and it shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem, and it shall not be quenched.

17.18.0.en: God asked Jeremiah to stand in the gate by which the kings of Judah, that is, the leaders of the people, and most of the people enter, for it is one of the gates of Jerusalem by which many enter, and it may be the Benjamin Gate; and He means that he should declare the following word to all the people, since they all pass, entering or leaving Jerusalem, by this gate and all the other gates, because the city of Jerusalem had many gates. The spiritual meaning of this is that we should declare the word of God to all who are around us and not to some only, and call everyone to be bound to the Church.

17.19.0.en: God's command through Jeremiah is not to work on the Sabbath day, whether by carrying goods from outside Jerusalem into it, that is, buying these goods, or by carrying loads from their houses to sell outside Jerusalem, but to hallow the Sabbath day and set it apart for the worship of God.

17.20.0.en: God declares with regret that His people refused to obey the commandment to keep the Sabbath, and their hearts were hard, so they were empty of every feeling of sonship toward God; and their disobedience is shown by the stiffness of their necks, as the unruly, rebellious animal refuses to have the yoke put on its neck and to submit to its owner; indeed they also murmured against God's discipline of them and did not understand that this was because of their sins.

17.21.0.en: He declares the blessings of obeying the commandment to keep the Sabbath in order to encourage them to keep it: that if they obey they will have great kings riding in chariots and on horses who will rule them, and they will live in peace and security; indeed He promises them not only rest in the earthly Jerusalem but also in the heavenly Jerusalem forever in the Kingdom of Heaven if they keep His commandments.

17.22.0.en: He completes the blessings that come from their obeying His commandments, that the Jews will come from every place, and He mentions here six regions to declare that from every place the believers will come and offer sacrifices of thanksgiving and holy worship to God.

17.23.0.en: And on the contrary, if they do not obey God's commandment, God allows the enemies, who are the Babylonians, to destroy Jerusalem and burn its gates and all its palaces.

17.23.1.en: Take care to obey the commandments of God, for they keep you from every evil, and you enjoy God's care for you and fellowship with Him on earth and then glories in heaven.

17.23.2.en: The potter and the plot against Jeremiah

18.0.0.en: Arise: it means hastening to carry out the command. It signifies the resurrection with Christ.

18.0.1.en: Go down: the potters most often made their workshops in the valleys to find clay suitable for their work, so He said to him, “go down,” that is, go down to the low valley. Going down signifies humility. God commanded Jeremiah to go to the potter's house, that is, one who works in making pottery, to hear the word of God, who provides an illustration for His word, namely the making of pottery.

18.0.2.en: And for a man to be able to hear the voice of God, he must be with Him, so that his life is renewed and he is able to be humble and hear and understand the word of God.

18.1.0.en: The wheels: the device on which the clay is shaped to make the pottery vessels.

18.1.1.en: When Jeremiah went to the potter's house he found him making a clay vessel on the wheel, and then he noticed that the vessel was marred; and it does not say that the potter marred it, because the potter signifies God and the clay vessel signifies men, who spoil their lives themselves by their distance from God. But God in His love reshapes the clay again and mends the vessel that was marred; for although it was marred, it is still in His hands, and if they repent and return to Him He renews their nature and makes them vessels of honor according to His good pleasure and what seems good to Him, as He renewed the human race by His redemption through the sacrament of Baptism.

18.2.0.en: When Jeremiah saw the potter's work as an illustration, God said to him: I am able, like this potter, to reshape you after you have spoiled your lives by sin, and to renew you. So He gives hope to His people that they may repent and return to Him, and He will restore them to their first sonship to Him and their pure life.

18.2.1.en: Trust in the power of God, who is able to renew your life however many or repeated your sins, for He is your Father who loves you and you are always in His hands; so return to Him in repentance and ask His help, and He will mend your life.

18.3.0.en: God declares His plan in dealing with men: if He finds them in an evil way of life, He decides that He will destroy them and pluck them up like trees, that is, kill them. This is not a final decision but a declaration of His anger at their evils, that perhaps they may repent and be delivered from this anger; and this shows the love of God, who wants all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth, and does not desire the destruction of anyone.

18.4.0.en: If this nation turns from its evil way of life and repents, God does not punish it; for what is meant by the evil that God would have brought upon it is its punishment.

18.5.0.en: The other case is that God promises the nation good, building up and blessings, and what is meant by planting is steadfastness, as the tree is fixed in the ground.

18.6.0.en: “In My sight:” any evil that a man does is against God and a defiance of Him.

18.6.1.en: “I will repent:” God speaks in human terms, which is to go back on what was decided; but in truth God knows everything before it is, and does not repent of anything, but He knows that He did not give them good because of their evils. So God's use of these words is like a grown person's use of words suited to children when he talks with them, not because he does not know the language of grown-ups but so as to be understood by the children.

18.6.2.en: If this nation leaves God and does sins before Him and refuses to obey His commandments, God does not do good to it and does not give it blessings.

18.6.3.en: Every wrong you do to others is directed against God, because all men are His image, and even if the sin is in your thought and in your heart, it is a defiance of God. Return to Him in repentance, for He is ready to forget all your sins.

18.7.0.en: Amend your ways: walk in the way of God and keep away from the ways of evil.

18.7.1.en: God warns His people of punishment for their sins, for divine decrees have been issued to punish them, that perhaps they may fear and return to Him, and He will lift this punishment from them.

18.8.0.en: Sadly, God's people answered Him badly, for they made light of His word and considered it vain, that is, worthless, and insisted on persisting in their evil thoughts and deeds; that is, they refused repentance and continued in sin.

18.9.0.en: God marvels at His people's rejection of His word, and the peoples of the world bear witness against them, who obey their pagan gods, whereas God's people, who ought to have been loving and clinging to Him, rejected Him and persisted in their evil; and He likens them to the virgin who has only her bridegroom, because she is not bound to any other man.

18.10.0.en: God rebukes His people that He loved them and gave them water in the form of snow on the tops of the rocks in the high mountains such as Lebanon, and when the snow melts it turns into flowing water that runs continually and waters man, animal and plant. So God gives them His heavenly blessings; why then do they not worship Him and thank Him? Why did they turn to the worship of idols?

18.11.0.en: The ancient paths: the ways of the fathers who lived with God and kept His commandments.

18.11.1.en: Paths: winding roads in the desert between the mountains, which are hard to travel.

18.11.2.en: Not cast up: a hard way that cannot be walked, which is the way of the worship of idols and evil. God continues His rebuke of His people, who neglected His blessings and forgot God's favors to them, who brought them out by a wondrous power from the land of Egypt and kept them in the wilderness of Sinai and fed them from heaven and gave them to drink from the rock. They left God, the Maker of good things, and went to burn incense to vanity, that is, the worship of idols, and the wicked caused the rest of the people to stumble, so they turned away from the straight ways of the fathers and walked in rugged ways that destroy them, which are the ways of the worship of idols.

18.12.0.en: Wag his head: shakes his head in mockery and grief.

18.12.1.en: I will show them the back: I will abandon them.

18.12.2.en: As a result of God's people's persistence in sin, God warns them of these punishments that they may repent, which are:

18.12.3.en: 1- Their cities will be demolished and their land will become desolate, and this was accomplished at the hand of Babylon; this signifies the loss of the possessions and desires to which the wicked man clings, and no one dwells in them, but there is heard in them the hissing of the winds, that is, their strong sound that moves with force because there are no walls or buildings.

18.12.4.en: 2- Every man who passes by these ruined cities, which perished because of their evils, will be astonished and mock. This signifies the demons' mockery of us when we persist in evil, so that we are cast into eternal torment.

18.12.5.en: 3- The inhabitants of Judah will be scattered like those pursued by a hot, violent wind, which is the east wind, and they flee lest they be suffocated by its heat; this signifies the cruelty of the wars of the demons that strike those who are far from God and the careless, scattering them and destroying them.

18.12.6.en: 4- The hardest punishment is God's abandoning them, so that He turns away His face, that is, His care for them, and leaves them to suffer afflictions because they rejected following Him and insist on that, so the afflictions are very severe upon them; and this signifies eternal torment.

18.12.7.en: When you see afflictions come upon you or upon others, know that they are warnings from God so that you turn from your sins, and when you ask God's help your eyes are opened and you see His blessings and thank Him, and your soul lives in you.

18.13.0.en: Shall not perish: shall not depart.

18.13.1.en: Smite him with the tongue: catch him in a word that condemns him, and punish him and kill him.

18.13.2.en: The people resisted the prophet Jeremiah because he prophesied the devastation of Jerusalem and their destruction, and they said that he was not a prophet because the word of God does not depart from the prophet, whereas Jeremiah does not speak the word of God but evil against the people; likewise he is not wise and has neither the Law nor counsel. Then they tried to catch him in a wrong word that he would say so that they could punish him for it, and thereby declare his words void so that no one would listen to him; that is, when they think his words are wrong by catching words against him, they make the people doubt him and not listen to his words. And in this they are not resisting Jeremiah only but rather God who sent him, and they reject His word.

18.14.0.en: Jeremiah calls on God for help to defend him against those who stand as adversaries to him and resist him, so that He hears their slanders and answers them.

18.15.0.en: Jeremiah marvels that his people answered his love with evil, for he stood before God asking mercy for his people, but they repaid his goodness with evil and wanted to kill him.

18.16.0.en: Bereaved: mothers whose children have died.

18.16.1.en: In the spirit of prophecy Jeremiah speaks of what will happen to his people, and not in a spirit of vengeance for what they say about him and their attempt to take revenge on him, because his fatherhood is clear throughout this book (Jer 14:17) (Jer 9:1) (Jer 8:21). So he prophesies the death of the young men and the men, and the women becoming bereaved and widows.

18.17.0.en: The people tried to kill Jeremiah by throwing him into a pit or catching him in their nets by trapping him with a word or trying to kill him by anything; therefore God takes vengeance on them by His divine justice, so Babylon attacks them, and cries come from all their houses for the death of many of them.

18.18.0.en: Jeremiah asks for divine justice for the evils of his people because of their counsel, so that they are punished with destruction. This is not only a prophecy but a declaration to the people, that perhaps they may repent, and he gains their souls because he loves them.

18.18.1.en: Do not resist the one who rebukes you, for it may be a message from God on his tongue, even if he increases the rebuke and blame; and if his word is wrong, make an excuse for him and do not take vengeance on him or wrong him.

18.18.2.en: The breaking of the earthen bottle
